eval.title: I Sold My Berkshire Stock

call.headline_quote: unfortunately for me for an expected return of 10 berkshire on a conservative basis is 50 over valued or 100 percent over valued and should crash 50

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: now we have 46 billion of earnings as a fundamental basis of our valuation

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: then the intrinsic value expecting a 10 discount rate is 468 billion for berkshire

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: if i take these calculations then my intrinsic value is much much lower and at 322 billion

what_is_priced_in.quote: currently the price earnings ratio on 36 billion is just below 20 but if we keep the market's price earnings ratio current at 20

reasons.claim: On a conservative growth and multiple assumption, Berkshire's intrinsic value is far below its market cap, implying it is overvalued for a 10% return.
reasons.quote: for an expected return of 10 berkshire on a conservative basis is 50 over valued or 100 percent over valued and should crash 50

data_check.gap_note: he says 322, as-of 4.33326e+11 (T0); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: market cap

reasons.claim: The stock price is up 60% on the same business, which mathematically lowers forward returns and raises risk.
reasons.quote: berkshire stock is up what is this 61 so 60 up on the same business berkshire is so big that it doesn't change in one year 60

data_check.gap_note: he says 60, as-of 286.82 (2021-06-11); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: A higher terminal multiple of 20 is unrealistic if interest rates rise, so he prefers a more conservative multiple of 15.
reasons.quote: if interest rates go up so will price earnings ratios go down and therefore 15 is much more conservative for a business

reasons.claim: Hidden earnings from equity stakes (like Apple's dividend/earnings gap) understate Berkshire's true earnings power, forming part of the valuation base.
reasons.quote: 3.22 billion is apple earnings that's not shown in berkshire's financial statement

data_check.gap_note: he says 8e+09, as-of 4.2521e+10 (FY2020); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: He finds a better opportunity elsewhere (Alibaba), with higher expected upside for similar quality and risk, so he moved capital out of Berkshire.
reasons.quote: i think alibaba has the potential to be a triple in the next five to ten years even more berkshire not therefore alibaba on the same margin of safety

external_facts_used: Charlie Munger's and Mohnish Pabrai's portfolio holdings not including Berkshire
Warren Buffett's Q1 earnings statement of about $7 billion
Apple's ownership stake (5.4%) and market value ($120 billion) held by Berkshire
Mohnish Pabrai's comments on adding to Alibaba position

critic.notes: Stance agrees (SELL). Minor issue: personal_action should be 'sold' — he explicitly states he sold his Berkshire B position, not 'none'.
